revocation_note: Open your account page, find the token under Your client tokens and select Revoke. The service refuses a revoked token on its next request. Revoking a token does not recall files that were already downloaded.

recipes.name: Codex
recipes.configuration_note: Merge this table into your existing config.toml. Do not replace your other settings. The Baltor-Step-Effects header says what your harness's steps may do with a Baltor item: read and write files in your project, run commands and use the network. Remove any effect your harness does not allow. Search still shows every item with the effects it declares; a download of an item that declares an effect you left out is refused, and the refusal names the effect.
recipes.verification_note: This command shows configuration, not a completed handshake. In a Codex session, inspect /mcp and confirm that Baltor's tools are available before asking it to search.
recipes.version_note: Documented configuration; native end-to-end qualification is pending. Check your installed version with codex --version.
recipes.removal_note: After the token is revoked, delete the mcp_servers.baltor table from config.toml and clear BALTOR_SERVICE_TOKEN from your environment.

recipes.name: Claude Code
recipes.configuration_location: A .mcp.json file in your project folder
recipes.configuration_note: Create this file, or merge the baltor entry into the mcpServers section of an existing one. Do not replace your other settings. The file holds the name of the variable, never the token, so it is safe to keep in version control. The Baltor-Step-Effects header says what your harness's steps may do with a Baltor item: read and write files in your project, run commands and use the network. Remove any effect your harness does not allow. Search still shows every item with the effects it declares; a download of an item that declares an effect you left out is refused, and the refusal names the effect.
recipes.verification_note: Run this command in your project folder, in the terminal where BALTOR_SERVICE_TOKEN is set. The list shows a status next to baltor. If the status is Pending approval, start claude in this folder once and approve the server. If the list warns about a missing environment variable, set the token before you start Claude Code. In a session, enter /mcp and confirm that Baltor's tools are listed.
recipes.version_note: Documented project configuration with environment variable expansion; native end-to-end qualification is pending. Check your installed version with claude --version.
recipes.removal_note: After the token is revoked, delete the baltor entry from .mcp.json and clear BALTOR_SERVICE_TOKEN from your environment.

recipes.name: Pi
recipes.configuration_location: Pi 0.73.1 extension: .pi/baltor.json beside .pi/extensions/baltor.ts. For Pi 0.99.2 native MCP, follow /docs/quickstart-pi.
recipes.configuration_note: This recipe targets Pi 0.73.1 through the Baltor extension. Pi 0.99.2 has built-in MCP; its native setup is documented at /docs/quickstart-pi. Save the extension this website serves at /assets/pi/baltor.ts as .pi/extensions/baltor.ts in your project folder, and read it first: Pi runs every extension in that folder with your permissions. Then create this file beside it. This file holds the name of the variable, never the token. The extension adds two tools, baltor_search and baltor_download. A download checks the published SHA-256 digest before it writes anything, then installs the skill in .pi/skills. step_effects says what your Pi steps may do with a Baltor item, and the extension sends it in the Baltor-Step-Effects header. Remove any effect Pi should not have. Search still shows every item with the effects it declares; a download of an item that declares an effect you left out is refused, and the refusal names the effect.
recipes.verification_note: Run this command in your project folder, in the terminal where BALTOR_SERVICE_TOKEN is set. It makes no model call. It shows whether the service answered, which account the token belongs to, and each installed Baltor skill with its digest check and whether Pi's skill loader accepts it. The last line says Result: ready. In a Pi session, enter /baltor for the same check.
recipes.version_note: Checked end to end with Pi 0.73.1 and Gemma 4 31B through Ollama Cloud on September 23, 2026: the model found and installed a Baltor skill with the two tools, and a new Pi session loaded that skill and used it. Check your installed version with pi --version.
recipes.removal_note: After the token is revoked, delete .pi/extensions/baltor.ts and .pi/baltor.json, and clear BALTOR_SERVICE_TOKEN from your environment. Installed skills stay in .pi/skills until you delete them. Their install records are in .pi/baltor/installed.

recipes.name: Baltor Harness
recipes.configuration_note: These are connection values for the Python protocol client, not a configuration file that the Baltor Harness loads automatically. Follow the linked guide to search, download and add the material to your task before running it. The engine does not select library material by itself yet. Keep only the step effects your task is authorized to use.
recipes.verification_note: This command checks the installation only. It does not contact Baltor and makes no model call. To check the library connection, search once with your token, download one item and compare its SHA-256 with the body_digest that the search returned. The two must be equal.
recipes.version_note: Works with one manual step. Checked on September 23, 2026 with loop-engine 0.1.0 from GitHub main: install, doctor, the Ollama Cloud route cloud.default, search, download with a digest check, and a task that used the downloaded item all ran. The engine does not search or download from Baltor by itself yet. Check your installed version with pip show loop-engine.
recipes.removal_note: After the token is revoked, clear BALTOR_SERVICE_TOKEN from your environment, delete the baltor entry wherever you copied these values, and delete downloaded material you no longer need. To remove the engine, delete its virtual environment and the ~/.loop-engine folder that holds its run records.
